call.sequence_note: Ran out of time and was rescheduled mid-presentation. The prospect flagged a hard stop at six o'clock after the training and nutrition pillars had been delivered; the accountability pillar, the delivery walkthrough, the commitment check and the price were all left for a second call booked for Wednesday at 4pm Central.

setter.evidence: Self-booked with no setter involved, from an Instagram ad the same morning: 'I came across that at this morning, I was rolling through the Instagram, and I just kind of booked the appointment, and I got the slot for today.' The internal operations walkthrough confirms that bookings without initials in the title are not sets.

prospect.name: Abdul Malik Mohammed
prospect.occupation: IT consulting, working from home and desk-bound from 8am. Works with a team in Colombia. Describes his work as stressful and often finishes around 5:30pm.
prospect.family_status: Married with five children. Sole earner — 'I'm the only main source of breadwinner in the family.' Self-describes as a big introvert and attributes it to not feeling confident about how he looks.
prospect.training_background: Overweight since childhood and never skinny at any point in his life. Long history of six-week bootcamps, done repeatedly, each producing roughly 20 lb of loss followed by full regain — has cycled between about 280 and 245 lb over several years. Best period was 2011 to 2012, training five days a week for two hours, but under-eating and taking no protein, which left him with loose skin he became insecure about. Has used personal trainers and disliked them — 'everything I feel like commercial, 30-minute session, you're done, and basically there is no checking back.' Holds a gym membership and managed one session last week and one or two a week on average over the last three months, mostly early on weekend mornings. Owns kettlebells at 10, 15 and 35 lb and has used them only at a basic level. Uses fasting, including dry fasting, as his main weight-loss lever. Was 253 lb a month ago and is now 268 to 270.
prospect.medical: High blood pressure, currently on medication, which he wants to come off — 'It got started on my BP, blood pressure medication, which I hate doing it. I hope I can reverse it back in some shape or form.' Diagnosed sleep apnea requiring CPAP, which he dislikes and was told may improve with weight loss. Knee problems for about two years that prevent jumping, jumping jacks and running. Shoulder pain for a couple of years with restricted overhead range. Chronic lower back pain that comes and goes, which he attributes to a weak lower back — 'anything that is not aligned, it's gonna get my back pain issue again, restarted.' Loose skin from previous weight loss. Roughly 36 BMI at 268 lb and six feet.

signals: Proposed label: the_cycler. Someone with a decades-long history of repeated short-programme successes followed by complete regain, whose blocker is maintenance and identity rather than knowledge, effort or willingness. Distinct from the_rebuilder, who lost ground once during a hard season and wants a former self back — this prospect has no former self to return to, having been overweight since childhood, and his best previous outcome ended badly with loose skin and insecurity. Distinct from the_prehab_fighter in that the conditions are chronic and managed rather than an acute event being fought.
The pattern is explicit and self-diagnosed: 'It's a rollercoaster ride for me. I lose 10-20 here and there and then gain it back again' and 'as soon as I stop, like boom, it comes back like rapidly'

Motivation is depleted by the history rather than absent — 'the biggest discouragement for me is just seeing my journey, like how I'm going to achieve that big goal' and 'you get to the point when you don't see as much results, then you kind of, you mentally, you get drained'

Correctly identifies his own missing mechanism as post-programme accountability: 'by the time that camp ends, obviously, there's no one holding you accountable at that point. And then you just let loose'

Worth clustering centrally — this shape is likely common in the corpus and none of the existing archetypes capture the repeat-relapse buyer, who is both the highest-intent and the highest-risk profile the offer encounters

goals.text: Lose about 80 lb, from 268 down to an ideal of 180 to 190
Come off blood pressure medication — named as his single biggest goal
Improve or resolve sleep apnea so he can stop using CPAP
Gain muscle while losing weight, specifically to avoid repeating the loose-skin outcome of 2011
Regain the strength he had in his twenties and stop stairs hurting his knees
Break the cycle of losing 10 to 20 lb and regaining it — wants something sustainable rather than another six-week sprint
Confidence — believes his introversion stems from how he looks and feels, and expects a change to carry into personal and professional life
Be more active with his five children and spend more time with them
Set a better example for his children than he currently does
Accountability — someone checking on him, which he names as the mechanism he has always lacked

pains.text: Hypertension requiring daily medication he resents taking
Diagnosed sleep apnea requiring CPAP, which he hates and which disrupts his sleep and feeds his blood pressure and stress
Regains all lost weight within weeks of stopping — 253 lb a month ago, 268 to 270 now
Knee problems for two years that rule out running and jumping, and make stairs painful
Chronic lower back pain and a weak lower back that flares whenever anything is misaligned
Shoulder pain for a couple of years with restricted overhead range
Sedentary all day from a desk at home, and too exhausted after work to train
Resignation about the size of the task — 'the big journey in front of me is the biggest discouragement right now'
Fear of repeating the loose-skin outcome, which made him insecure the last time he lost significant weight
Accountability vanishes when a programme ends and he immediately lets loose
Stressful work that drains any remaining motivation in the evenings
Identifies as big-boned and lifelong overweight, which he treats as structural — 'never been skinny in my life to begin with'

offer.guarantee_mentioned: Mentioned in passing during the training pillar, before any price: 'We actually have a guarantee in our program, which I think you'll actually like this, where we're going to add at least eight kilograms to some of the main kettlebell lifts by the end of the program, or Trevor will continue coaching you for free until you do.' Stated without the three-of-five-lifts qualifier or any of the eligibility conditions.

evidence: No price was presented and no offer was made. The call ended before the accountability pillar and the delivery walkthrough.
Prospect called the hard stop: 'One quick thing, Michael, I, you have to get going here. Six o'clock. have to drop, but we can continue to learn.'
Rescheduled on the call with an invite sent live: 'we said Wednesday, 4 p.m. Okay. So I just sent you that there. I'll text you the morning of just to confirm that time still works.'

Counter-evidence, positive: strong engagement throughout, and when asked what stood out he gave a substantive answer — 'rather than just going to the gym, you're going to set up your foundations with this. I think that is something I'm more interested to learn' and 'I would love to hear more about it for sure.'

Counter-evidence, negative on lead quality: booked from an Instagram ad the same morning with no product knowledge at all — 'I know nothing about him, to be honest with you' — and had not watched any of the material sent to him.
Homework set for the gap: the rep re-texted the content page and asked him to watch it before Wednesday.
outcome.next_step: Second call booked for Wednesday 2026-07-08 at 4pm Central, with a confirmation text on the morning. The accountability pillar, the delivery walkthrough, the commitment check and the price all remain to be covered. Prospect to watch the content page beforehand.

notable.note: By some distance the best discovery in this batch, and the most clinically exposed prospect in it. The baseline, past-attempts and consequence-frame work were all genuinely strong — the rep pinned down actual training frequency rather than accepting the self-report, asked what the prospect ate yesterday meal by meal rather than accepting 'my diet is pretty clean', ran the script's self-accountability challenge almost verbatim, and pushed past the first vague answer on the two-year question, which he did not do on any other call in the batch. What was done with the medical picture is the problem. Hypertension on medication, sleep apnea on CPAP, two years of knee problems that rule out jumping and running, a shoulder with restricted overhead range, and chronic lower back pain were all asked about properly, including duration, and then never referenced again except to predict that 'the stuff with the knees, like a lot of that's going to start going away in a very short period of time.' No clearance question was asked. Two things to the rep's credit that should not be lost: he took explicit permission before the confrontational section, and when the prospect asked for the one thing the programme genuinely cannot deliver — gaining enough muscle to avoid loose skin across an 80 lb loss — he said so plainly rather than selling around it. Also worth recording: the prospect asked twice for material to review between calls and there is none, and the pillar he most needed to hear, accountability, is the one the call ran out of time before reaching.

quality.notes: Continuous inversion. Long stretches of the rep's speech appear under the prospect's label, including most of the confrontational identity passage from 00:27:45 onward, the entire training pillar and the intermittent-fasting section at 00:46:05. Several turns fuse both speakers with no break, and the baseline exchange around 00:07:24 attributes the rep's health-conditions question to the prospect. Roles resolved from content: the rep is whoever asks the questions, delivers the pillars and controls the calendar.
